foraging-guide-text:
De Artibus Rusticis: Foraging Guide
Where to roughly look for new crops in the wild.
Note that seeds for vegetables and legumes can also be found in cracked vessels.

Bearleek
Bearleek is found in forests with a moderate climates.

Chives
Chives are found in meadows with a moderate climate and fair amount of rain.

Peas
Peas are found in meadows with a moderate climate.

Garlic
Garlic is found in meadows and forests with a somewhat warmer temperature and a fair amount of rain.

Horseradish
Horseradish is found in meadows and forests with a moderate climate.

Leek
Leek is found in forests with a moderate climate and a fair amount of rain.

Beetroot
Beetroot is found in meadows with a moderate climate and a fair amount of rain.

Lentils
Lentils are found in meadows with a warmer climate.

Lettuce
Lettuce is found in meadows with a warmer climate and a fair amount of rain.

Favabeans
Favabeans are found in meadows with a warmer climate.

Cucumber
Cucumbers are found in meadows with a warmer climate and a fair amount of rain.

Anise
Anise is found in forests with a temperate climate.

Black Cumin
Black Cumin is found in meadows with a warmer climate.

Chervil
Chervil is found in forests with a moderate climate.

Cress
Cress is found in forests with a warmer climate.

Eruca
Eruca is found in meadows with a warmer climate.

Tarragon
Tarragon is found in meadows with a moderate climate.

Meum
Meum is found in forests with a moderate climate.

White Mustard
White Mustard is found in forests and meadows with a warmer climate.
herbs-guide-title: De Artibus Rusticis: Herb Harvesting Guide
herbs-guide-text:
De Artibus Rusticis: Herb Harvesting Guide
Time is of the essence if you want a bountiful harvest.
Harvest crops by right-clicking, which obtains you edible greens and sets back growth. This will preserve the plant and enable repeated harvests if done at the right time. In general, once a plant blooms, its leaves become bitter and inedible. After this, you can usually wait for the plant to mature and harvest another product.

Anise
Harvest anise in growth stage 5 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 4.

Bearleek
Harvest bearleek in growth stage 4 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 3.

Chives
Harvest chives in growth stage 5, 6, or 7 to obtain greens. Stage 7 will yield extra chives and seeds, while still allowing future harvests. Resets the growth to stage 3.

Chervil
Harvest chervil in growth stage 4 or 5 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 3.

Cress
Harvest cress in growth stage 3 or 4 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 2.

Eruca
Harvest eruca in growth stage 4 or 5 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 3.

Estragon
Harvest estragon in growth stage 5, 6, or 7 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 4.

Meum
Harvest meum in growth stage 4 or5 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 3.

White Mustard
Harvest white mustard in growth stage 5 to obtain greens. Resets the growth to stage 4.

Garlic
Garlic cannot be harvested by right-clicking. Depending on its growth stage, you will receive greens, bulbs, or both.
Stage 4 & 5 will yield garlic greens but no bulbs.
Stage 6 will yield a few greens and bulbs.
Stage 7 yields many bulbs but no greens.
cooking-guide-text:
De Artibus Rusticis: Cooking Guide
Be creative with your harvest.
Note that most new food items used by this mod can be added to most meals as either ingredients or seasoning. One herb and two portions of spice can be combined into a spice blend, noticeably boosting satiety.

Broths
While it is not a meal in itself, you may make six different types of broth to enhance your soup or use it to make mash.
Fish broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, fish, fishbones, and seasoning.
Herb broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, and either three herbs, or two herbs and some spice.
Meat broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, a piece of red meat, and seasoning.
Marrow broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, two bones, and seasoning.
Chicken broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, a piece of chicken, and seasoning.
Vegetable broth: In a cooking pot, combine two liters of water, two vegetables, and seasoning.

Composte
While its name does not sound pleasant, the meal received its name from the Latin term ‘componere’, which means to combine. It was meant to be served as a side dish and strike a balance between sweet and sour. Take 0.2l of alcohol, one fruit, and two pickled vegetables to create this meal.

Mash
Mash was a staple of daily medieval cuisine. Take 2 carrots, turnips, parsnips, pumpkins, peas, lentils, fava beans, horseradish, beetroots, or leeks, and combine them with 0.2l of oil, or 1.0l of chicken broth, herbal broth, or vegetable broth. Lastly, add some flour as a thickener.

Poached Greens
In vino veritas. In wine there is truth. Take one to three pieces of romaine lettuce or herbs and poach them in a liter of alcohol, honey or some broths. You may add seasoning, pears, apples, or fish.

Sauerkraut
The longest-lasting meal you can make with De Artibus Rusticis. Take two to three pieces of pickled cabbage, some honey or wine, and either add a piece of red meat, a vegetable, an apple, or seasoning.

Meum Pear Honey
Meum pear honey is more of a remedy than a meal. Mix 0.5l of honey, one pear, and one meum root to create this remedy. Additionally, you may add seasoning. Regardless of ingredients used, it will always restore 5.0 health.
